summary: Negotiated per-model rate not honored for mixed-model batch embedding job — unexpected invoice line
description:
Issue summary:
Customer MapFlow Analytics reports a finalized invoice line that billed their mixed-model batch embedding job at the default hosted rate instead of their negotiated per-model rate for gptx-3.7-alpha. The batch included records sent with model aliases and a single job id; they expected the gptx-3.7-alpha segments to be billed at the contracted rate ID: MR-2025-GPTX.

Impact:
- Customer saw a ~$1,250 unexpectedly higher charge on the monthly invoice (Invoice #MF-202602).
- This is blocking reconciliation for their finance team and raising concerns about rate enforcement for mixed-model jobs.

Environment:
- Production (us-east-1).
- Customer using self-serve plan with a negotiated per-model override applied to model alias "gptx-3.7-alpha" via contract MR-2025-GPTX.
- Batch job submitted via client SDK v1.9.2 on 2026-02-20, job id: batch-9876-mf.

Steps to reproduce (from customer):
1) Create a mixed-model batch with 120k records where 60% routed to rwkv-large-v1 and 40% to gptx-3.7-alpha via model aliasing in a single job.
2) Submit as a single multipart request using key X-API-Key: ak_live_mapflow_01.
3) Allow processing to complete and wait for hourly postback to billing pipeline.

Expected behavior:
- Billing should apply contracted per-model rate to tokens generated by gptx-3.7-alpha segments (rate ID MR-2025-GPTX).
- Invoice line should split or annotate amounts so negotiated portion is visible.

Actual behavior:
- The finalized invoice aggregated the entire job under the default hosted embedding tariff for self_serve plan. No per-model override lines were present.

Logs / evidence attached by customer:
- invoice_pdf: MF-202602.pdf (customer provided PDF excerpt)
- usage_export.csv: shows job id batch-9876-mf with token counts and model_alias column populated
- SDK request snippet showing model aliases and single job id

Initial hypothesis:
- Postback aggregator may have collapsed multi-model segments into a single rate bucket when requests used a single job id and model aliases, losing the per-model override key during tag propagation.

Requested outcome:
- Adjust invoice to reflect negotiated rate for gptx-3.7-alpha portion or issue a credit for the delta.
- Root cause explanation and a mitigation plan to prevent re-occurrence (e.g., ensure per-model rate tags survive batching/reconciliation).
comments: Support - Priya Kapoor (2026-02-28): Acknowledged receipt, escalated to billing reconciler. Asked customer for usage CSV and invoice PDF. Requested permission to share with revenue ops.

Customer - Elena Ruiz (MapFlow) (2026-03-01): Uploaded MF-202602.pdf and usage_export.csv. Confirms negotiated rate applied in contract and SDK shows model_alias column. Asks for provisional credit while investigating.

Billing Eng - Jonah Park (2026-03-02): Noted similar aggregation behavior seen in nightly reconciler logs when job contains 'job_id' and multiple model_alias entries. Opened INT-2819 to follow internal fix.
Support - Liam O'Connor (2026-03-03): Requested trace ids linked to postback window for 2026-02-20 02:00-04:00 UTC and asked SRE to pull reconciler run #20260220-03.

SRE - Mikaela Grant (2026-03-04): Provided reconciler run excerpt: reconciler collapsed model_alias tag when canonical_rate_id was not present on microbatch rows. Pointed to code path in reconciler v2.11 that performs implicit aggregation. See GH PR linked.
investigation_notes: Reconciler aggregated postbacks for batch-9876-mf and applied rate lookup at the job-level. Microbatch rows had model_alias but missing canonical_rate_id due to SDK behavior when aliasing within a single job payload. The rate-override lookup occurs after aggregation, which caused default tariff application. Reproducer created locally with SDK v1.9.2 and reconciler v2.11. Fix candidate: propagate canonical_rate_id at microbatch creation or perform rate-resolution before job-level aggregation.
resolution_notes: Provisionally issued credit to MapFlow Analytics for the overcharged amount (credit MF-C-20260305 = $1,250). Finance notified and invoice MF-202602 marked for adjustment. Deployed reconciler patch to v2.11.1 that resolves canonical_rate_id earlier in pipeline. Added a reconciliation test for mixed-model batch jobs. Customer notified and CC'd on internal PR and release notes. Close action items: INT-2819 to monitor next billing run, add docs for SDK model aliasing recommended pattern.
qa_verification_steps: 1) Re-run reconciler locally against saved usage_export.csv: ensure microbatch lines include canonical_rate_id.\n2) Run end-to-end billing pipeline in staging for mixed-model job: verify invoice split lines and applied rate IDs.\n3) Confirm monthly billing run for March does not show similar mis-applied defaults for MapFlow and two other test tenants.
final_status: Provisional credit applied; fix deployed to reconciler v2.11.1; monitoring in place
resolution: Credit issued and reconciler patch deployed
